record.summary: A development-focused continental AI strategy with a focus area on minimising AI risks. It names bias and discrimination, disinformation and manipulation of political systems, surveillance, deepfakes, cyber threats and military uses, and calls for technical standards on the safety and security of AI systems. It recommends agile, risk-based regulation, AI governance bodies and independent oversight institutions in member states, a regional AI Ethics Board to review novel large-scale AI systems, impact assessments, transparency registers, red-teaming, a centre of excellence on AI safety and security and an annual AI safety and security conference.
record.notes: Adopted by the AU Executive Council at its 45th Ordinary Session in Accra, Ghana, on 18-19 July 2024; the AU document page is dated 9 August 2024. The foreword and executive summary speak of five focus areas and fifteen action areas, while section 2.4 lists six focus areas, the sixth being an inclusive governance and regulatory framework. Implementation is planned for 2025-2030: a first phase in 2025-2026, a mid-term review in 2027 and a second phase from 2028. The AU publishes the strategy in English, French, Arabic and Portuguese.
record.scope_note: Mainly a development strategy for harnessing AI's benefits, building capabilities and attracting investment, with minimising risks as one of its focus areas; included as the African Union's continental AI strategy, whose governance and safety recommendations are addressed to all member states.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026. Stored: the AU document page on au.int (11 and 18 Oct 2026; only the site's news ticker differs between the two copies), the English strategy PDF (66 pages) and the French PDF, both from au.int (11 Oct 2026). The English PDF confirms the title, the July 2024 date, adoption by the Executive Council at its 45th Ordinary Session on 18-19 July 2024, its preparation under the AU Commission's Commissioner for Infrastructure and Energy, and the content of the summary and notes; the AU page confirms the endorsement, gives 9 August 2024 as its own date and links the English, French, Arabic and Portuguese texts. The Arabic and Portuguese PDFs are not stored. No Executive Council decision number appears in the stored files.

summary.locator: page 37, High-Level Recommendations for AI Governance and Regulation
summary.quote: Promote agile, forward -looking and r isk-based regulations at national and regional levels that foster accountability and transparency in the design and deployment of AI Systems.

Support Member States to establish independent institutions to conduct oversight on the use of AI, enforce compliance with standards as they emerge, and provide access to redress and remedy where violations occur.

Establish a regional independent AI Ethics Board, which reviews applications from AI research groups seeking to develop novel, large-scale AI systems with the potential to impact African societies significantly.
Provide incentives for citizen -led solutions that identify and mitigate AI biases and high-risk issues within AI systems, such as AI Bounty Contests and Red -Teaming efforts.
Adopt algorithmic or AI transparency registers to publicly list AI systems being used in Member States

This ranges from cyber threats to AI applications in disinformation for manipulation of political systems and societies to Generative AI-produced and distributed information, which can be fully automated through untraceable deepfakes.

judgment.status_reasoning: Adopted by the AU Executive Council at its 45th Ordinary Session on 18-19 July 2024 as a strategy that member states are urged to domesticate through national strategies; its implementation period runs from 2025 to 2030 with a review in 2027, and the AU page still offers it in four languages on 18 Oct 2026. Nothing stored shows it replaced or withdrawn. Published (non-binding, current).
judgment.scope_reasoning: An intergovernmental AI strategy with a focus area on minimising risks and governance recommendations to all member states; in scope, with a scope_note because its main focus is development and capabilities.
judgment.date_reasoning: The strategy's title page reads 'July 2024' and the acknowledgment dates the Executive Council's adoption to its two-day session of 18-19 July 2024, so no single day can be given; 2024-07 is kept. The AU page's 9 August 2024 is its own posting date and goes in the notes.
judgment.topics_reasoning: Unchanged and supported: risk-based classification (risk-based regulation), deepfakes & synthetic media, national security & military (military domain, peace and security), evaluation & testing (impact assessments, red-teaming), accountability & liability (oversight institutions, redress, AI Ethics Board), international cooperation (regional coordination and global AI governance).
